1.explanation: All Perl regex matching support in highlight.js lives in the anonymous default export function in src/languages/perl.js. In that function, the PERL_DEFAULT_CONTAINS array defines two regexp containers. The second container – with begin: /(m|qr)?\// – only matches m or qr followed by a slash, so patterns like m(/…/) or m#…# or m{…} are not recognized. To fix the bug, this export function needs to be updated: its regexp container definitions must allow arbitrary delimiters for m and qr operators, not just slashes.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a Perl code snippet being highlighted by highlight.js. The line “$d .= '/' if $d !~ m(/$);” uses the m operator with a slash-delimited regex. However, only the literal '/$' is highlighted as a string, not recognized as a full regex. The highlighter fails to detect m-style regex when the delimiter is not the default slash or when arbitrary delimiters (e.g. m|…|, m#…# or m{…}) are used.

2.explanation:
Within the default export function in perl.js the PERL_DEFAULT_CONTAINS array defines a ‘regexp’ container with:
  begin:   /(m|qr)?\//
  end:     regex.concat(/\//, REGEX_MODIFIERS)
This only matches regexes delimited by '/', so any m operator with other delimiters (|, #, {, etc.) won’t be recognized. To fix the bug, this rule must be extended to detect the full m<delim>…<delim> syntax, not just m/…/.
2.bug_scenario: In the user’s screenshot, an m‐style regex using slash delimiters (m(/$)) is not being highlighted correctly. The highlighter only understands m// and doesn’t allow m with other delimiters (|, #, {, etc.), so constructs like m|/$| or m#/$# also fail.
